title.narrative: Localizing and mainstreaming the NUA and SDGs in Ciudad Juárez

description.narrative:
The municipality of Juárez is located in the state of Chihuahua, north of the Mexican Republic. Ciudad Juárez is its municipal seat and is also the main urban center of the entity. It is located on the border line with the Rio Grande and shares a binational border with El Paso, Texas.
In 2015, the total area of the municipality of Juárez was 3,577.7 km², of which 330.8 km2 (9.2% of its territory), made up its urban area. Its urbanization index is almost total, 99.6%, which is why it is considered a highly dynamic and densely populated municipality. From 2000 to 2015, Juárez experienced disorderly city growth. The urban area has expanded by 40%. With a density of 42 inhab./ha, the development model promoted so far has caused the inhabitants of Juárez to have to invest more time and resources to get around, in addition to not having adequate conditions of public transport and road infrastructure.
According to the CPI calculation, Juárez has moderately weak prosperity (51.21). This value is below the national average of the basic CPI (53.74 / 100). In 2017 the city had almost 1.4 million inhabitants, of which 37.8% lived in poverty. According to data from Coneval, by 2015 39.9% of the population received income below the welfare line, 14.5% suffered from deficiencies due to educational backwardness, and 13.7%, due to access to food. 85 areas have been identified that require priority attention to reduce poverty conditions, located in the west and southeast of the city.
Ciudad Juárez has an average of 5.6 m2 / hab of green area. According to the 2016 Sustainable Urban Development Plan, in Juárez around 20% of the urban area corresponds to vacant land, a situation that fosters conditions of insecurity, violence and a discontinuous urban image.
This project will promote a more robust implementation of the New Urban Agenda and SDGs at the local level planning in Ciudad Juarez, with a gender approach. To do so, the following outcome and outputs are proposed:
• Outcome 1. Long-term oriented urban planning instruments and projects developed to achieve a sustainable urban development a) Output 1. 2030 City Vision. This seeks to define in a participative way the desired future for the city, taking into account its comparative advantages and setting a roadmap, in a consensual and evidence-based way, towards where the urban development of Ciudad Juárez should evolve. The city vision will include the definition of a strategic framework made up of territorialized objectives, goals and lines of action, as well as recommendations for their materialization around the pillars of the NAU; urban legislation, municipal economics and finance, and planning. b) Output 2. Strategic projects portfolio. Based on the lines of action of the strategy and the inputs of the Vision diagnosis, the project will identify which are the areas that concentrate the greatest opportunities in the territory to propose interventions aimed at improving urban conditions. For the prioritized project, its implementation strategy, both spatial and programmatic, will be defined in detail. For this, a dossier will be integrated that delimits its territorial actions and integrates a cost-benefit analysis to determine if the investment of the project is appropriate on the costs associated with its realization, in terms of social, environmental and economic benefits. Recommendations on urban design, financing and management will be included for its execution. After the integration of the portfolio is an opportunity to prioritize a project to submit or link with the CIF initiative.
• Outcome 2. Improved capacities and resources in Ciudad Juarez for the localization of NUA and SDGs. a) Output 3. Participatory public space strategy. UN-Habitat proposes the development of an urban planning strategy for the intervention of public spaces at the neighborhood scale, based on participatory processes with neighbors, workers, visitors and passers-by from an inclusion perspective that considers the integrated gender approach, life cycle, disability and interculturality. A methodology for the intervention and design of public spaces from participatory planning processes will be generated. The inclusion of women and youth is particularly relevant to the output due to the municipality’s context. For this output it is considered relevant to work closely with the Public Space Global Programme and using the City-wide assessment tool, among other methodologies. b) Output 4. Tactical urbanism plan. UN-Habitat proposes the development of a tactical urban planning master plan that allows the collaborative identification of sites with the potential to be intervened with actions of agile implementation, low cost and broad impact for the community, from a broad process of involvement that allows the generation of co-responsibility with the actors, the appropriation of the interventions and their sustainability.
